extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure only.
- **Deployment path:** GitHub Actions (`Deploy to Azure`) with triggers on **`push`** and **`workflow_dispatch`**.
- **Runtime/runner:** `ubuntu-latest` hosted runner.
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** No regions, availability zones, multi-region, or failover controls are represented in the provided data. Resilience posture cannot be confirmed from this configuration.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret store in use:** `github_actions_secret`.
- **Observed secret usage:** Azure credentials are referenced as `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`.
- **Risk note:** The credential material is stored in GitHub Actions secrets rather than a cloud-native identity flow. No plaintext secret is shown in the config, but the design still depends on a long-lived secret being available to the workflow.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption-at-rest coverage:** `false` in the aggregate signals.
- **Key management:** No customer-managed key (CMK), Key Vault, or other key management controls are shown.
- **Implication:** There is no evidence of at-rest encryption coverage from the provided configuration, and no explicit encryption/key management posture can be validated.

### 4) IAM / least-privilege
- **IAM type:** `managed_identity`
- **Principal:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`
- **Scope:** `subscription`
- **Trust principals:** `github-actions`
- **OIDC:** `uses_oidc: false`
- **Risk note:** The trust relationship is broad at the **subscription** scope, which is typically more permissive than necessary for CI/CD deployment workflows. Because OIDC is not used, the workflow depends on a secret-backed credential rather than short-lived federated identity. The provided data does not show any least-privilege scoping at resource-group or resource level.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runner model:** GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest`.
- **OIDC:** Disabled.
- **Trigger surface:** `push` and manual `workflow_dispatch`.
- **Risk note:** `push`-based deployment increases blast radius if branch protections, review controls, or commit integrity checks are weak. The use of hosted runners means execution occurs in a shared GitHub environment; no hardened self-hosted runner controls are present in the data.

### 6) Container security
- **No container nodes were provided.**
- Therefore, there is **no evidence** to assess root/non-root execution, health checks, or resource limits from the supplied configuration.

### 7) Key risks and recommendations
1. **Replace secret-based Azure auth with OIDC federation.**  
   Move from `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` to GitHub-to-Azure federated identity to eliminate long-lived credentials in GitHub Actions.

2. **Reduce IAM scope from subscription-wide access.**  
   Re-scope deployment permissions to the minimum required Azure resource group / resource level and validate the effective actions granted to the workflow principal.

3. **Close the encryption and resilience gaps.**  
   Confirm encryption-at-rest is enabled for all deployed data/services and define explicit region/zone or failover posture for the Azure deployment.

## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry points**
  - `FastAPI` calls four API endpoints: `Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, and `Chat Endpoint`.
  - `Bearer Auth` protects `Chat Endpoint`, `Generic`, `Login`, `Logout`, and `Me`.

- **Orchestration**
  - `OpenAI Agents` calls all five agents: `Triage`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`, and `Cancellation`.
  - `Triage Agent` delegates to `Flight Status Agent` and `FAQ Agent`.

- **Agent-to-tool access**
  - `Triage Agent`, `Cancellation Agent`, `FAQ Agent`, `Flight Status Agent`, and `Seat Booking Agent` all call the same tool set:
    - `Baggage Tool`
    - `Cancel Flight`
    - `Display Seat Map`
    - `Faq Lookup Tool`
    - `Flight Status Tool`
  - `OpenAI Agents` also directly calls tools including `Lookup Reservation` and `Update Seat`.

- **Models and guardrails**
  - All listed agents use `gpt-4.1-mini`.
  - `Relevance Guardrail` and `Jailbreak Guardrail` both use `gpt-4.1-mini`.
  - The graph shows no explicit connection from the guardrails to the chat or agent flows, only that they exist and use the model.

- **Data stores**
  - `Sqlite` is present but has **no connections**, so no data flow to it is shown.

- **Security observations**
  - Several tools appear reachable without a visible guardrail boundary around tool invocation.
  - `OpenAI Agents` has broad direct access to tools, including `Lookup Reservation` and `Update Seat`, which are not tied to a specific agent in the graph.
  - No datastore access is shown, so sensitive storage exposure is not indicated by this graph.
